title: A tech can still cancel a payment and change a closed ticket's bill, which the round-1 fix meant to block
description: Round 1 (8b3e5f2) made removePayment owner/admin-only ("like voiding a register sale"). It also stopped a TECH from calling removeLine on a closed ticket ("only the owner or an admin can change its bill"). Both controls can be sidestepped. addPayment (line 353) uses requireUser and only rejects 0 (`if (amount == null || amount === 0)`), so any role can enter a negative payment that cancels an earlier one. addLine (line 264) has no closedAt or role check, so a TECH can add a DISCOUNT, a negative FEE or a negative-priced SERVICE/PART line to a COLLECTED ticket. The scan station (src/actions/scan.ts:61) only adds to tickets in OPEN_STATUSES, so the bench form is the odd one out.
failure_scenario: The owner rings up ticket #51 for $129 by card and sets it to Collected. A TECH opens the ticket and gets the expected errors from 'Remove line' and 'Remove payment'. The same TECH then records a payment of -129.00 CASH and adds a Discount line on the closed ticket, and both are accepted. With a -$129 cash payment plus a $129 discount, the ticket shows a $0 balance and the month's CASH total drops by $129. That hides $129 taken from the drawer, which the admin-only removal was meant to prevent.
suggested_fix: In addPayment, reject amount < 0 unless user.role !== 'TECH', or send refunds and corrections through an admin-only path, the same as removePayment. In addLine, apply the removeLine rule: `if (t.closedAt && user.role === 'TECH') throw new UserError('The ticket is closed: only the owner or an admin can change its bill.')`. Also consider refusing negative SERVICE/PART/FEE prices for TECH.
evidence:
Playwright as TECH qa-secbw-tech@test.local on the COLLECTED ticket cmuin4lyj0002qq7dq18scnja (own throwaway shop, instance on :6733):
TECH remove line: The ticket is closed: only the owner or an admin can change its bill.
TECH remove payment: Only the shop owner or an admin can change this.
TECH negative payment: Payment recorded
(addLine DISCOUNT 50 on closed ticket -> ok)
DB afterwards: status COLLECTED, closedAt set; lines SERVICE 12900, DISCOUNT -5000; payments CARD 12900, CASH -12900 'oops'.
Code: `export const addPayment = safe(async function addPayment(...) { const user = await requireUser(); ... if (amount == null || amount === 0) throw ...` and addLine has only `const t = await ownTicket(user.shopId, ticketId);` with no closedAt/role check.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The code matches the claim. addLine (tickets.ts:264-331) only calls ownTicket and never checks closedAt or role. addPayment (tickets.ts:350-364) uses requireUser and rejects only null or 0. So a TECH can change a COLLECTED ticket's bill: a DISCOUNT line, or a negative SERVICE line that has the same effect as removing a line. That is exactly what round 1 (8b3e5f2) blocked in removeLine, so the round-1 lock is incomplete. I rate it medium, not higher. It is an intra-shop insider bypass that leaves visible rows. Negative ticket payments have existed since the first commit as the refund path, and a TECH can already pay out a refund of any amount at the register: completeSale accepts a custom line with negative qty and has no role check. What is new is the closed-bill edit, plus the fact that Payment has no userId, so the negative payment cannot be traced to who entered it.
also_reported_as: security: src/actions/tickets.ts:357 A tech can reverse a payment or change the bill of a closed ticket, working around the round-1 admin-only rules
security: src/actions/tickets.ts:353 TECH can add discount lines and negative payments to closed/paid tickets, bypassing the owner/admin gates on removeLine and removePayment
code: src/actions/tickets.ts:357 A TECH can still change a closed ticket's bill and cancel out a recorded payment, getting around the round-1 owner-only controls
qa: src/actions/tickets.ts:357 Negative payments are accepted, so a tech can void payments despite the admin-only removePayment rule; the invoice prints "--$159.00"

title: addLine accepts Infinity or huge quantities and hours: stock becomes -Infinity then NaN, ticket balance shows $NaN
description: The PART and LABOR branches of addLine parse numbers with Number() and only check the minimum. `Math.max(1, Math.round(rawQty || 1))` passes Infinity through, and LABOR only checks `hours > 0`, which Infinity and 1e300 pass. qty is a Float column, so Postgres stores Infinity. The part's stock is then decremented by Infinity to -Infinity. Removing the line later increments by Infinity, giving NaN, which later +/- adjustments cannot repair. Ticket totals become Infinity/NaN, and those values flow into the sales report and the job.update snapshot sent to partners. The register (register.ts:176) checks `Number.isFinite(qty) && |qty| <= 10000` and the scan station caps at 999; the bench path has no cap. saveCustomer has the same gap (records.ts:309 `Number(commission)`, no finite or 0-100 check), and DISCOUNT has no cap, so a discount larger than the bill makes the invoice negative.
failure_scenario: A tech (or a mistyped or pasted value) enters qty 'Infinity' for stocked part QA-INF-1 (10 on hand), or labor hours '1e300'. Both are accepted. The part shows -Infinity on hand, and after the line is removed it shows 'NaN on hand'. The ticket page shows 'Balance $NaN', and the low-stock list, sales page and partner bill all carry the bad numbers until someone runs a manual shelf count.
suggested_fix: Validate every numeric input in addLine the same way completeSale does. Require Number.isFinite; cap PART qty at 1..10000 (yards 0.125..10000) and LABOR hours at 0<h<=100 or similar. Bound unit prices (e.g. |price| <= 10_000_000 cents) and cap a DISCOUNT at the current pre-discount total. In saveCustomer, require 0 <= commissionPct <= 100 and a finite number.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The PART branch's Math.max(1, Math.round(rawQty || 1)) and LABOR's `hours > 0` both let Infinity and 1e300 through. Postgres float8 stores Infinity, so stock becomes -Infinity, and removeLine then makes it NaN. ticketTotals gives NaN, which shows on the ticket and would poison the month's sales totals. Only a signed-in user of the same shop can do it, and it needs a deliberate non-finite input. It can be undone with a stock count (parts.ts:91-94 sets an absolute qty) and by removing the line. Rated medium as missing validation that stores bad data. One side note is misplaced: the saveCustomer commission code is at records.ts:96/104, not 309.
also_reported_as: code: src/actions/tickets.ts:292 Ticket lines accept unbounded or non-finite quantities, hours and prices: one line turns the ticket, Invoices and Sales totals into $NaN or $Infinity

title: Reopening a closed ticket keeps its old closedAt, warrantyUntil and readyAt, which skews the sales log, the warranty and the storage-fee warning
description: setStatus only ever sets readyAt, closedAt and warrantyUntil, keeping the first value (`t.readyAt ?? now`, `t.closedAt ?? now`, `!t.warrantyUntil`). Moving a ticket back to an open status (mis-click, customer returns it, repair failed) never clears them. Consequences: (1) the Sales log counts COLLECTED tickets by closedAt (sales/page.tsx:18), so a ticket collected in September after a stray COLLECTED or ABANDONED in August is billed to August; (2) the warranty runs from the first, wrong collection; (3) the invoice prints 'Returned <date>' while the machine is on the bench; (4) removeLine still treats the reopened ticket as closed, so techs can't fix its bill; (5) the dashboard storage-fee 'overdue' warning uses the first readyAt after the machine went back on the bench.
failure_scenario: Owner sets ticket #7000 to COLLECTED by mistake and then back to ON_BENCH. The DB still has closedAt and warrantyUntil set, the invoice header says 'Returned Sep 26, 2026', and a TECH trying to remove a line gets 'The ticket is closed: only the owner or an admin can change its bill.'
suggested_fix: In setStatus, when the new status is in OPEN_STATUSES clear closedAt (and warrantyUntil if it was set by that close). When leaving the READY statuses for ON_BENCH, WAITING_* or IN_TRUCK, clear readyAt. On a later close, set closedAt and warrantyUntil fresh. Optionally keep a status history (events) for the audit trail.
evidence: Reproduced: after COLLECTED then ON_BENCH, `select status, closedAt, warrantyUntil` shows ON_BENCH | 2026-09-26 17:04:31 | 2026-12-25 17:04:31. Playwright (TECH): toast 'The ticket is closed: only the owner or an admin can change its bill.'; invoice header 'Invoice #7000 Received Sep 26, 2026 Returned Sep 26, 2026'. Code lines 146-150 set these fields only when entering READY or closed statuses and never clear them.
verifier_notes: confirmed: setStatus (tickets.ts:140-155) only ever sets readyAt, closedAt and warrantyUntil, keeping the first value, and never clears them when the ticket moves back to an open status. StatusSelect (ticket-controls.tsx:21-27) saves on change, with no confirm step, so a stray pick of COLLECTED or ABANDONED is realistic. After a reopen: sales/page.tsx:18 counts COLLECTED tickets by the stale closedAt (wrong month); warrantyUntil runs from the first close and is printed on the invoice (invoice/page.tsx:112); the invoice prints 'Returned <date>' (line 38) while the machine is on the bench; removeLine:335 still treats the ticket as closed; the dashboard overdue check (page.tsx:40) uses the first readyAt. The reviewer's DB state matches this.
also_reported_as: qa: src/actions/tickets.ts:146 Moving a ticket back to an earlier status keeps readyAt/closedAt, which causes false storage-fee alarms, 'Returned' on a reopened invoice, and locks techs out
security: src/actions/tickets.ts:146 Reopening a closed ticket keeps closedAt/readyAt/warrantyUntil: the tech stays locked out, and sales and storage-fee dates are wrong

title: Saving a ticket's text overwrites every field from a stale form: a second user's approved amount and notes (or a partner shop's relayed approval) are silently erased
description: saveTicketText writes all eight fields (serviceRequested, problem, diagnosis, workDone, notes, preApprovedCents, approvedCents, techId) from whatever the browser submits, with no version or updatedAt check. Two people with the same ticket open overwrite each other without any warning. The partner flow makes this likely: when the sewing shop answers an estimate, the job.reply handler (partners.ts ~800) writes ticket.approvedCents and appends a line to ticket.notes. A tech who has the ticket open and then clicks Save sends the old notes and a blank approved amount, which erases both.
failure_scenario: The tech opens ticket #0054 and starts typing a diagnosis. Meanwhile the owner enters 'Customer approved ($) 250' and the note 'Customer called 2pm: OK up to $250, replace bobbin case only', and saves. The tech then saves the diagnosis and gets a 'Saved' toast. The approved amount and the note are now gone (both NULL).
suggested_fix: Send the ticket's updatedAt with the form and update with `where: { id, updatedAt }` (optimistic concurrency). If the ticket changed, return a UserError such as 'Someone else changed this ticket, reload'. At minimum, write only the fields that changed. Keep partner-relayed notes in a separate field or log that this form does not submit.
evidence: s16.js with two browser contexts: 'db after owner: 25000|Customer called 2pm: OK up to $250, replace bobbin case only' -> tech clicks Save -> 'db after tech: ||Timing slipped, hook retimed' (approvedCents and notes both NULL). Code: tickets.ts:165-177 unconditional `db.ticket.update({ where: { id: ticketId }, data: { ..., notes: str(formData.get("notes")), approvedCents: toCents(formData.get("approved")), ... } })`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: saveTicketText (tickets.ts:157-179) writes all eight fields from the submitted form with no version or updatedAt check. The fields are uncontrolled inputs with defaultValue in a form that is never remounted, so a page open from before another change submits the old values. The partner job.reply handler (lib/partners.ts:803-811) writes ticket.approvedCents and appends to ticket.notes in the background. A tech who then saves the Status and work form erases both, and no warning is shown. This is a silent lost update in a multi-user flow.
also_reported_as: code: src/actions/tickets.ts:165 Saving the ticket text form overwrites the customer's approval that partner sync wrote to the ticket (lost update on approvedCents and notes)

title: A tech can still change a closed ticket's bill by adding discount, negative-fee or negative-price lines (round-1 lock only covers removing lines)
description: Round 1 (8b3e5f2) made removeLine refuse TECH users on a closed ticket ("The ticket is closed: only the owner or an admin can change its bill."). addLine has no such check: after ownTicket() it goes straight to creating the line. A TECH can therefore lower a closed and fully paid bill however they like, with a DISCOUNT line, a FEE with a negative amount, or a SERVICE/PART with a negative price (toCents accepts negatives). That is the same result the lock is meant to prevent. addPayment and saveTicketText have no closed check either.
failure_scenario: The owner bills a Bernina (service $159, tax 8.25%), takes $172.12 by card and sets the ticket to COLLECTED (closedAt is set). A TECH opens it. Removing the service line is refused. Adding the fee/discount form with Discount of $100 succeeds, and the bill drops to $63.87 total on a closed ticket. The sales log's collected service and tax figures change with it.
suggested_fix: Put the closed-ticket rule in one helper, e.g. `assertBillEditable(ticket, user)`, and call it from addLine, removeLine and addPayment (and from the approved/pre-approved amounts in saveTicketText if those count as the bill). Reject negative prices for SERVICE/PART/FEE in addLine: discounts should only be possible through the DISCOUNT kind.
evidence: Ran as a TECH (qa-bench-a-tech) on closed ticket #0053: 'remove line: [The ticket is closed: only the owner or an admin can change its bill.]', then 'add discount: []' (no error). The ticket went from 'Subtotal $159.00 | Tax $13.12 | Total $172.12' to 'Subtotal $59.00 | Tax (8.25%) $4.87 | Total $63.87'. DB: DISCOUNT | tech discount | -10000. Code: addLine (tickets.ts:264-267) calls `const t = await ownTicket(user.shopId, ticketId);` and never checks t.closedAt, while removeLine (tickets.ts:335) has `if (line.ticket.closedAt && user.role === "TECH") throw ...`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: The claim is accurate and the round-1 fix is incomplete. removeLine (tickets.ts:335) refuses TECH users on a ticket with closedAt set, and its error says only the owner or an admin can change the bill. addLine (tickets.ts:264-329) calls ownTicket() and never checks closedAt or role. The fee/discount form, the service price and the part price all go through toCents, which accepts negative values, so a FEE or SERVICE line can carry a negative price. The ticket page shows every add-line form to every role, so this is reachable from the normal UI. Neither prior round touched addLine's authorization (9ba25a4 changed only saveMeasurements in tickets.ts). The actor is an employee of the same shop and the new lines show on the ticket, so this is medium, not high.

title: Timing and tension readings are silently dropped: negative mm specs (189 settings), '85 g' and '22,5' are discarded, and an existing value is wiped, with a 'saved' toast
description: grams() returns null for anything that isn't a plain non-negative number. saveMeasurements uses it for mm/degree timing readings and skips those fields. saveTension writes null over the stored value. Neither returns an error, so the UI says 'Timing readings saved' / 'Readings saved'. 189 of 13,505 measurable factory settings have negative ranges (e.g. Bernina B 570 QE 'Hook drive belt tensioner position' -0.5 to 0 mm, Melco X home -0.4 to 0.4 mm), so valid readings for them can never be recorded. A tech who types the unit ('85 g', which matches the 'g' placeholder) or a decimal comma loses the reading, including one saved earlier.
failure_scenario: On a Bernina B 570 QE ticket the tech enters -0.3 as found and -0.2 as left for 'Hook drive belt tensioner position' and clicks Save timing readings. The toast says 'Timing readings saved', but after a reload both fields are empty (measurements = {}). Upper-as-found was saved as 85, then re-entered as '85 g' and saved. 'Readings saved' appears and upperFoundG is now NULL.
suggested_fix: Use a separate parser for mm/deg readings that allows negatives. Strip a trailing unit and accept a decimal comma. Return a UserError that names the field when a non-empty value can't be parsed, instead of saving null or skipping it.
evidence: s7.js: 'timing save: [Timing readings saved]', 'tension save 2: [Readings saved]', 'after reload: timing found= "" left= "" upper found= "" bobbin found= ""'; DB `measurements={}, upperFoundG=NULL, bobbinFoundG=NULL`. SQL: `select count(*) filter (where valueMin<0 or valueMax<0) ... where unit in ('mm','deg')` -> 189 of 13505. Code: tickets.ts:193-198 `return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? n : null;` used at 206-209 and 223.
verifier_notes: confirmed: grams() (tickets.ts:193-198) returns null for negatives and for any non-numeric text like '85 g' or '22,5'. saveMeasurements (line 223) uses it and skips those fields, then rebuilds the whole measurements object from what is left, so any earlier value for that setting is lost. saveTension (206-209) writes null over the stored reading. Neither action throws, so safe() returns ok and ActionForm shows the success toast. The inputs are plain text with inputMode=decimal and no min, so negatives and units can be typed. 189 of 13,505 measurable mm/deg factory settings have negative ranges, so a valid reading for them can never be saved. Prior rounds did not touch grams().

title: Trade-account commission % isn't validated: '10%' saves as NaN, silently pays $0 commission and shows 'NaN' in the form
description: saveCustomer stores `Number(commission)` without checking it. '10%', '10 %' or '1O' become NaN (Postgres float8 accepts it), and negative or >100 values are also accepted. ticketTotals uses `commissionPct ? ... : 0`, and NaN is falsy, so every ticket through that quilt shop silently earns $0 commission on the ticket page, the customer page and the sales log, with no error. `kind` is also cast without a check (an unknown value makes Prisma throw, giving a generic error).
failure_scenario: Owner adds trade account 'QA Quilt Shop' with commission '10%'. It saves without error; the DB has commissionPct = NaN and the edit form shows 'NaN'. Commission on its collected tickets reads $0 until someone notices.
suggested_fix: Parse with the same strip-% logic users expect, require Number.isFinite and 0 <= pct <= 100, and throw UserError('Commission is a percent between 0 and 100.'). Validate kind against ['RETAIL','TRADE'].
evidence: Reproduced: Playwright custForm = 'NaN'; DB `QA Quilt Shop | TRADE | NaN`. Code: `commissionPct: kind === "TRADE" && commission != null ? Number(commission) : null`; ticket-math.ts:26 `commissionPct ? Math.round((service * commissionPct) / 100) : 0`.
verifier_notes: confirmed: saveCustomer (records.ts:104) stores `Number(commission)` without validation. A natural input like '10%' becomes NaN, and Postgres float8 accepts it. ticketTotals (ticket-math.ts:26) then treats the NaN as falsy and reports $0 commission on the ticket page (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:81), the customer page (customers/[id]/page.tsx:33) and the Sales log 'Shop commission owed' (sales/page.tsx:37,79), with no error. Negative values and values over 100 are accepted too. A normal input gives a silently wrong money figure. It can be fixed by re-editing, because commission is recomputed on each view, so it rates medium.
also_reported_as: qa: src/actions/records.ts:104 Trade-account commission typed as '10%' is stored as NaN; that account's commission is then silently $0 everywhere

title: Invoices 'Unpaid' tab and 'Still owed' total silently leave out every unpaid ticket older than the latest 500
description: The page loads the 500 highest-numbered tickets that have lines (`orderBy: { number: "desc" }, take: 500`) and only then filters by balance in memory. Once a shop has more than 500 billed tickets, which takes a few months for a busy bench, older unpaid invoices disappear from the Unpaid tab. The 'Still owed' and 'Billed' totals are understated, and the page can say 'Nothing owed. Every invoice is paid.' Old debts such as abandoned machines and trade accounts that pay late are exactly the ones this view is for. Nothing on the page says the list is truncated.
failure_scenario: Shop has 506 billed tickets. #1 is unpaid ($100) and #2-#506 are paid. /invoices?show=unpaid shows 'Invoices shown 0, Still owed $0.00' and 'Nothing owed. Every invoice is paid.' Searching q=1 finds the $100 unpaid invoice.
suggested_fix: Do the balance filter in SQL, e.g. a raw query or a view that computes line and payment totals per ticket and filters balance > 0 before LIMIT. Or keep an owed/paid flag on Ticket, updated by addLine, removeLine and addPayment. Paginate instead of silently cutting at 500, compute 'Still owed' with an aggregate over all tickets, and show 'latest N' when the list is limited.
evidence: Seeded my throwaway shop B (SQL: 506 tickets, one $100 line each, payments on #2-#506). Playwright: unpaidCards ['INVOICES SHOWN 0','BILLED $0.00','STILL OWED $0.00'], unpaidEmpty=1; with &q=1: ['INVOICES SHOWN 1','BILLED $100.00','STILL OWED $100.00']. Code: lines 23-44 `take: 500` then `.filter(({ tot }) => (show === "unpaid" ? tot.balance > 0 : ...))`. The customers list (customers/page.tsx:28, take 500, alphabetical) is also cut off without notice.
verifier_notes:
confirmed: invoices/page.tsx:23-44 loads the 500 highest-numbered billed tickets and only then filters by balance in memory. Once a shop has more than 500 billed tickets, older unpaid tickets fall off the Unpaid tab, and the 'Still owed' and 'Billed' totals omit them. The page can then show 'Nothing owed. Every invoice is paid.' and nothing says the list is truncated. This is the only shop-wide unpaid view. The other 'owed' figure (customers/[id]/page.tsx:30) is per customer. I rated it medium, not high: this is a read-only report, the stored data and per-customer balances stay correct, and it only starts after 500 billed tickets. That is a shop of a few months, though, and the invoices it hides are the old debts this view is for.
confirmed: invoices/page.tsx:23-44 loads the latest 500 tickets that have lines (orderBy number desc, take 500) and only then filters Unpaid/Paid in memory. 'Invoices shown', 'Billed' and 'Still owed' are sums over those filtered rows, and the page gives no sign that the list is cut off. Once a shop has more than 500 billed tickets, any unpaid ticket older than the latest 500 drops off the default Unpaid tab, and 'Still owed' is understated. It can even show 'Nothing owed. Every invoice is paid.' The file has not changed since 16192ac, so neither review round touched it. I rated it medium, not high. Only a reporting list view is affected: per-ticket balances, /sales and stored data are all correct. Searching by invoice number, customer or serial still finds the ticket, and the customer page (customers/[id]/page.tsx:30) computes owed over all of that customer's tickets. It still hits every established shop, since 500 billed tickets comes in a few months, and it hides exactly the old debts the view exists to chase, so it is more than cosmetic.
also_reported_as: qa: src/app/(app)/invoices/page.tsx:40 Invoices page takes only the latest 500 billed tickets before filtering, so 'Unpaid' and 'Still owed' silently leave out older unpaid invoices

title: Photo upload reads a chunked body of any size into memory (the size check only looks at the Content-Length header)
description: The route's early 413 check relies on the Content-Length header (`Number(req.headers.get('content-length') ?? 0) > MAX_BYTES + 100_000`). A request sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked has no Content-Length, so it passes. `await req.formData()` then reads the whole body into memory before `file.size > MAX_BYTES` is checked. Route handlers have no framework body limit (the 16 MB serverActions.bodySizeLimit does not apply to them). Any signed-in user can use this, and on a hosted install with ALLOW_SIGNUP anyone who signs up can, to exhaust the memory of the one server process every shop shares. /api/library/file/route.ts:41 and /api/figures/route.ts:10 use the same header-only pattern (outside this review's scope).
failure_scenario: A signed-in user streams a 200 MB multipart body with chunked encoding to POST /api/photos. The server reads all of it and only then returns 413. In the test the process RSS rose from 318 MB to 1 GB for one request, so a few parallel requests would get a Railway container OOM-killed and take every shop offline.
suggested_fix: Do not trust Content-Length alone. Reject requests without Content-Length (411) or count bytes while reading req.body (a ReadableStream reader that aborts past MAX_BYTES + overhead) before parsing multipart. Put the same limited reader in a shared helper for /api/library/file and /api/figures. A per-shop photo quota would also help.
evidence:
Own instance on :6733, signed in as qa-secbw-a:
VmRSS before: 318112 kB
--- with Content-Length (4MB): Photo is too large (3 MB max). [413 0.024969s]
--- chunked (no Content-Length) 200MB: Photo is too large (3 MB max). [413 2.730522s up=209741017]
VmHWM: 1002856 kB  VmRSS: 1002856 kB
(command: node gen.js 200 | curl -b jar -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -H 'Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----qaBoundary' --data-binary @- http://localhost:6733/api/photos)
verifier_notes: confirmed: proxy.ts's matcher excludes /api, so nothing buffers or limits the body before the handler runs. The route's only early check reads the Content-Length header. A chunked request has no Content-Length, and req.formData() buffers the whole multipart body before file.size is checked. serverActions.bodySizeLimit does not apply to route handlers. Any signed-in user can do this, including anyone who signs up on a hosted install with ALLOW_SIGNUP, and it grows the memory of the one process all shops share. Rated medium: a DoS that needs auth.
also_reported_as: code: src/app/api/photos/route.ts:12 The photo upload size limit is skipped by a chunked request body: the whole upload is read into memory before the 3 MB check
qa: src/app/api/photos/route.ts:12 The photo upload size guard only checks the Content-Length header; a chunked request streams any size into memory before the 3 MB check

title: Clearing or lowering 'Next ticket number' rewinds the counter, and on a busy shop every check-in then times out
description: num() turns a blank field into 0 (Number("") === 0), so `Math.max(1, Math.round(num("nextTicketNumber", ...)))` stores 1. Any lower number, or a stale Settings tab saved later, is also accepted. saveShop rewrites nextTicketNumber on every save, even when only the phone changed. createTicket (tickets.ts:104-106) and partner job intake (partners.ts:1062-1064) then step past used numbers one at a time: an UPDATE plus a SELECT per number, inside an interactive transaction with Prisma's default 5 s timeout. With a few thousand existing tickets the transaction expires and rolls back, the counter never moves, and every later check-in fails the same way.
failure_scenario: The owner clears 'Next ticket number' (or types 1) and clicks Save shop, and the toast says 'Saved'. With a few thousand tickets (fewer on Railway, where each query is slower), the next 'Check in a machine' runs for more than 5 s and the page is replaced by 'This page couldn't load'. The counter stays at 1, so no tech can check in any machine until someone fixes the setting. With fewer tickets, new tickets instead get low numbers (0001, 0002...) out of order with the paper log.
suggested_fix: In saveShop, treat a blank field as 'keep the current value' and refuse a number at or below the highest existing ticket (`SELECT max(number)`) with a UserError. Only write nextTicketNumber when the field actually changed from the value the form loaded. In both allocation loops, jump straight to max(number)+1 when the counter hits a used number instead of stepping one at a time.
evidence: Shared app, shop A: blank next ticket #, warranty, abandoned -> toast ["Saved"], DB `nextTicketNumber` 51 -> 1, warrantyDays 90 -> 0, abandonedAfterDays 60 -> 0. Private DB: 6000 tickets numbered 1..6000, counter 1. /tickets/new header 'Next ticket number: 0001'. Submitting a check-in ended with 'This page couldn't load A server error occurred.' Server log: `Transaction API error: A query cannot be executed on an expired transaction. The timeout for this transaction was 5000 ms, however 5002 ms passed`. DB afterwards: nextTicketNumber still 1, ticket count still 6000.
verifier_notes: confirmed: saveShop (settings.ts:43) maps a blank field to 0 via num(), because str() gives null and Number("") is 0, then Math.max(1, ...) stores 1. Lower numbers are accepted as well. createTicket's allocation loop (tickets.ts:102-106) then steps past each used number with an UPDATE plus a SELECT inside an interactive transaction that has Prisma's default 5 s timeout. With a few thousand tickets the transaction expires and rolls back, the counter never advances, and every check-in fails. Each failed try also leaves behind a newly created customer/machine, because those are created before the transaction. With gaps in the numbering (a shop that started at its paper-log number), new tickets instead get low out-of-order numbers. A small stale-tab rewind is harmless (the loop skips), so the damage needs a large rewind on a shop with many tickets: medium.

title: Shop settings save negative or absurd tax, labor, markup and day values; '8.25%' is silently dropped
description: num() accepts any finite number, maps blank to 0, and silently falls back to the old value for anything unparseable. toCents() accepts negatives and values beyond the Int column. Nothing checks ranges. The tax rate is copied onto every new ticket (tickets.ts:120) and register sale (register.ts:245), and ticketTotals computes tax as taxBase*taxRatePct/100, so a bad rate produces wrong money on every sale. abandonedAfterDays=0 flags every ready machine as abandoned with the storage-fee notice (page.tsx:40,68). The partner terms already clamp this value to 14-365 (partner-terms.ts:63); shop settings don't.
failure_scenario: An admin types '-5' for sales tax: every new ticket and register sale subtracts 5% tax. They type '8.25%': the toast says 'Saved' but the old rate is kept. '1e6' is stored as 1,000,000%. Labor '-45' is stored as -$45.00/hr. Labor '99999999' overflows the Int column and the Settings page is replaced by 'This page couldn't load', losing what was typed.
suggested_fix: Use one parser for these fields: blank keeps the current value; strip '%', '$' and ','; reject NaN with a UserError naming the field; enforce ranges (tax 0-25, markup 0-1000, warranty and abandoned days 0-3650 or 14-365, money 0 to $100,000). Make toCents callers reject negatives and anything over 2^31-1.
evidence: Shared app, own shop A via the Settings UI (DB after each save, columns tax|next#|warranty|abandoned|laborCents|tz): tax "-5" -> ["Saved"] `-5|...`; tax "8.25%" -> ["Saved"] still `-5`; tax "1e6" -> ["Saved"] `1000000`; labor "-45" -> ["Saved"] `-4500`; labor "99999999" -> no toast, pageerror 'An error occurred in the Server Components render', body 'This page couldn't load A server error occurred. Reload'. The shop was restored afterwards.
verifier_notes: confirmed: saveShop has no range checks. num() silently falls back to the old value for anything Number() can't parse, and toCents has no bounds. The most concrete case: a new shop's taxRatePct defaults to 0 (schema.prisma). An owner who types '8.25%' gets the toast 'Saved', and the field still shows 8.25% because the input is uncontrolled and not reset. The DB keeps 0%, so every new ticket and register sale charges no sales tax without any sign of it. A negative rate is stored and copied onto tickets and sales (tickets.ts:120, ticketTotals uses it as-is). A labor rate beyond Int range throws an unhandled Prisma error. This is missing validation that stores bad data and gives wrong money: medium.

title: 'Invoice (on account)' is recorded as a payment: the trade account's debt disappears, the printed invoice says Balance due $0.00, and the Sales log counts it as money taken
description: The ticket page's payment method list (tickets/[id]/page.tsx:471, from PAYMENT_LABEL) offers INVOICE 'Invoice (on account)', which means billed to the trade account and not yet paid. addPayment stores it as an ordinary Payment of the full balance. Everything downstream treats it as money received. ticketTotals.paid includes it, so the balance becomes 0. The Invoices 'Unpaid' tab and 'Still owed' drop the ticket. The customer page's 'owed' goes to 0. The printed invoice lists 'Paid <date> (Invoice (on account)) -$X' and 'Balance due $0.00'. The Sales log 'Money taken' (sales/page.tsx:30) adds it in. No receivable exists anywhere else, so what dealers owe the shop becomes invisible once a ticket is put on account. If the dealer's real payment is recorded later, the ticket shows a credit and 'Money taken' counts the sale twice.
failure_scenario: A quilt-shop trade account's machine is collected, and the tech records the $180 bill as 'Invoice (on account)' and prints the invoice to send to the dealer. The invoice says 'Balance due $0.00', the ticket leaves Unpaid invoices, and the month's 'Money taken' includes $180 that hasn't arrived. When the dealer pays, recording it gives a -$180 balance and $360 'taken'.
suggested_fix: Don't count INVOICE (and arguably SHOP_COLLECTED) as cash. Either exclude them from `paid` and 'Money taken' and show them as 'On account' owed by the via-account, or remove INVOICE from the payment methods and add an 'on account' status per ticket, with a trade-account statement where real payments settle it.
evidence: constants.ts:54 INVOICE label; tickets.ts:353-365 addPayment stores any method as a Payment; ticket-math.ts:21-22 paid = sum of all payments, balance = total - paid; invoices/page.tsx:43 filters Unpaid by balance > 0; customers/[id]/page.tsx:30 owed from balance; tickets/[id]/invoice/page.tsx:95-105 prints each payment and 'Balance due'; sales/page.tsx:30 taken = sum of every payment amount. No code path treats INVOICE differently (grep finds only the label).
